title: Hybrid films loaded with 5-fluorouracil and Reglan for synergistic treatment of colon cancer via asynchronous dual-drug delivery

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Figure 6 contains duplicated XRD patterns, meaning the same data appears multiple times, suggesting either an error in figure preparation or potential data manipulation. This was confirmed by an official 2025 corrigendum published by the journal (doi: 10.3389/fbioe.2025.1597014) which corrected the XRD patterns without changing the paper's conclusions. predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract (release mechanism claim) vs Section 3 Results (drug controlled release mechanisms)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract states: 'The controlled release mechanisms were shown to be an erosion mechanism for Reglan and a typical Fickian diffusion mechanism for 5-FU.' This unqualified claim conflicts with the Results section, which reports release exponents n = 0.323 (Fickian, S2 homogeneous particles), n = 1.24 (S3 core-shell particles), and n = 1.12 (S4 hybrid film). Only the intermediate product S2 follows Fickian diffusion; the final dosage form S4 and core-shell particles S3 are classified as Super Case II transport (n > 0.89). The abstract's blanket 'typical Fickian diffusion mechanism for 5-FU' overgeneralizes to the actual final product. The paper partially self-reconciles in the conclusion by noting the Korsmeyer-Peppas equation 'fails to predict nanomaterials with complicated chamber structures,' but the abstract omits this important caveat. Additionally, an internal tension exists: Section 15 classifies S3/S4 as Super Case II transport while Section 16 describes 5-FU release 'through diffusion,' which are mutually exclusive transport regimes.

summary:
The paper 'Hybrid films loaded with 5-fluorouracil and Reglan for synergistic treatment of colon cancer via asynchronous dual-drug delivery' (doi: 10.3389/fbioe.2024.1398730, published 13 June 2024 in Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology) was verified in exhaustive mode with lenient strictness. The paper was segmented into 28 snippets (21 sections, 3 tables, 1 equation, 1 figure compilation, 1 keywords, 1 metadata section) and verified by four specialist verifiers.

Two issues were identified:

1. FIGURE DUPLICATION (confidence 0.85): Figure 6 contains duplicated XRD patterns. This is the most significant finding and was independently confirmed by a 2025 corrigendum (doi: 10.3389/fbioe.2025.1597014) published by the journal, which corrected the XRD patterns without changing the paper's scientific conclusions. The existence of an official corrigendum validates this finding and means the error has already been addressed by the authors and journal.

2. ABSTRACT-RESULTS INCONSISTENCY (confidence 0.70): The abstract claims a 'typical Fickian diffusion mechanism for 5-FU' as a blanket statement, but the Results section shows only the intermediate homogeneous particles S2 (n=0.323) follow Fickian diffusion, while the final hybrid film S4 (n=1.12) and core-shell particles S3 (n=1.24) exhibit Super Case II transport. The paper's conclusion partially reconciles this by noting the Korsmeyer-Peppas model's limitations for complex chamber structures, but the abstract lacks this qualification. An additional minor internal tension exists between Sections 15 and 16 regarding diffusion vs. Super Case II terminology.

All other aspects of the paper were verified cleanly: Equation 1 (LE% formula) is mathematically correct (confidence 0.95); spot-checked citations (Peppas 1985, Shen et al. 2020, Alfatama et al. 2024) all exist and are correctly attributed (confidence 0.95); drug amounts, particle diameters, LE values, and regression parameters are internally consistent across sections. The text sections show no critical logical contradictions, unsupported claims, or invalidating methodology flaws.
